Modern.tagline: Round-yoke sweaters at the right gauge.
Modern.brandNameRationale: The circular yoke is the structural shoulder construction of the Lopapeysa, the Bohus, and modern top-down sweater design. The gauge is the foundational measurement — stitches per inch — that every garment depends on. Paired with an ampersand they ground the brand entirely in knit-trade vocabulary.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern knitwear has split between mass-import sweaters and a small considered-knit cohort of independent designers. The opening is for a brand that puts the circular yoke and the gauge swatch in the brand position and builds a small permanent catalog from yoke-led designs.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Andrea Mowry (drea.renee.knits) holds the considered-modern knit-designer slot. Brooklyn Tweed (brooklyntweed.com) sits in the design-led yarn-and-pattern tier. Quince & Co. (quinceandco.com) plays the considered-modern peer. We sit closer to Brooklyn Tweed with a sharper yoke focus.
Modern.positioningStatement: A modern knit brand organized around the circular yoke and a published gauge.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 55. Knits one sweater a year. Reads Pom Pom Quarterly. Will rip back twenty rows to fix a gauge error.
behaviors: Knits a swatch before the sweater
Re-knits the same yoke in three colorways

dos: Publish the gauge with every pattern
Name the wool and the spinner

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark — Yoke & Gauge set in a calm modern grotesk, with a small circular-yoke geometry mark beside the word. The mark alone is the favicon.

typography.primary: GT America for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: GT America Mono for gauges and yarn weights
typography.rationale: One family. Mono carries the technical knit data.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: The Aran Islands (Galway, Ireland) gave the world the Aran cable-and-bobble sweater; the Hebrides (Outer, Scotland) gave the world Harris Tweed and Hebridean wool. Paired with an ampersand, the two place-anchors signal a hand-knit brand rooted in two of the great British and Irish wool islands. Both are public-domain geographic references.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury knitwear at the hand-knit tier serves the buyer who wants one cardigan a year, made by a named knitter, from named wool. The product is a single garment per commission, finished by hand, signed by the maker.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Inis Meáin (inismeain.ie) is the institutional Aran-luxury benchmark. Harley of Scotland (harleyofscotland.com) holds the considered-Scottish slot. Jamieson's of Shetland (jamiesonsofshetland.co.uk) is the Shetland-luxury peer. We sit between Inis Meáin and Jamieson's with a hand-knit specialty.
Luxury.positioningStatement: Hand-knit cardigans and pullovers from named knitters on the Aran Islands and the Hebrides.

targetAudience.primary: 50 to 75. Owns at least one Inis Meáin piece. Travels to Ireland or Scotland each spring. Pays for the wool and the hands.
behaviors: Names the knitter on the garment label
Re-orders the same cable pattern in three colors

dos: Name the knitter and the island

Luxury.logoDirection: A serif wordmark — Aran & Hebrides set in a classical roman with a small embossed cable-knit mark. The mark appears on every garment label and on the printed island monograph.

typography.primary: Canela for the wordmark and the island monograph
typography.secondary: Adobe Garamond for body and commission documents
typography.rationale: Canela carries the island-heritage display tradition. Garamond keeps documentation warm.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: A skein is the loose coil of yarn the spinner ships before it's wound into a ball — single archaic trade word, six letters, terminal period. The brand is the unit of yarn itself.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimal yarn brands have converged on jewel-tone marketing. The opening underneath is a yarn shop stripped to the unit of trade — the skein — sold in undyed and naturally dyed colorways with the spinner named on every label.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Brooklyn Tweed (brooklyntweed.com) holds the considered-American spinner slot. De Rerum Natura (dererumnatura.fr) sits in the considered-French peer position. Tukuwool (tukuwool.fi) plays the Finnish naturally dyed peer. We sit closer to Tukuwool with a sharper single-skein framing.
Minimal.positioningStatement: Naturally dyed and undyed yarn, sold by the skein, with the spinner named.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 55. Knits two sweaters a year. Owns a yarn swift. Reads ply structure on the label.
behaviors: Weighs every skein before casting on
Re-orders the same dye lot in three colors

dos: Name the spinner and the breed
Print the yardage and the ply

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark only — Skein. set in a calm humanist sans, lowercase, terminal period. A small twisted-skein mark serves as the favicon.

typography.primary: Neue Haas Grotesk for the wordmark and body
typography.rationale: One face. The brand is the skein, not the type.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: Fair Isle is the small Shetland island whose colorwork knitting tradition became the generic name for two-color stranded knitting worldwide — public-domain geographic and technique term. Mills closes it as a serious knitwear manufacturer at trade scale.
Corporate.industrySummary: Knitwear manufacturing is a serious B2B category. The buyers are heritage outdoor brands, department stores, and uniform programs. The vendors compete on yarn sourcing, gauge consistency, and on-time delivery across thousands of garments.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Johnstons of Elgin (johnstonsofelgin.com) is the institutional Scottish knit-mill benchmark. Hawick Knitwear (hawickknitwear.com) holds the contract-knit slot. William Lockie (williamlockie.co.uk) is the heritage-mill peer. We sit smaller, sharper on the Fair Isle and stranded-colorwork specification.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Contract knitwear manufacturing in the Fair Isle and stranded-colorwork tradition.

targetAudience.primary: 45 to 60. Heads of Sourcing and Production at heritage outdoor brands, department stores, and uniform programs.
behaviors: Specifies by yarn weight and gauge
Requests sample sweaters before the order

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small geometric mark — a stranded-colorwork pattern reduced to two crossing strokes. FAIR ISLE MILLS set in a tight modern grotesk, suitable for B2B spec sheets and trade-show banners.

typography.primary: Inter for marketing and B2B materials
typography.secondary: Source Serif Pro for printed gauge books and RFPs
typography.rationale: Inter scales clean across digital. The serif handles printed mill documentation.

Creative.brandNameRationale: Wool-gathering is the idiom for daydreaming — the mind wandering as the hands knit — and the literal act of collecting wool from hedgerows in the British wool trade. The pun runs both ways. The brand sits on the pleasure of the slow craft.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative knitting brands have crowded the social-media-pattern space. The opening underneath is for a brand that treats knitting as a slow daily practice, with a printed annual journal of patterns, essays, and dye-day notes.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Pom Pom Quarterly (pompommag.com) holds the design-led-quarterly slot. Laine Magazine (lainepublishing.com) sits in the considered-Nordic-knit-publication tier. Making Magazine (makingzine.com) plays the considered-craft-journal peer. We sit beside Laine with a sharper essayist's voice.
Creative.positioningStatement: A creative knit brand publishing an annual pattern-and-essay journal in the wool-gathering tradition.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 55. Reads about knitting between rows. Owns the Elizabeth Zimmermann books. Will spend a year on one sweater.

dos: Tell the story between the pattern and the wool
Name the dye day and the dyer
donts: Use the word craft as marketing

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark — Wool Gathering set in a warm humanist serif with a small drawn mark of two hands lifting a tangle of yarn. The hands alone are the favicon.

typography.primary: GT Sectra for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: GT America for body and pattern instructions
typography.rationale: Sectra carries the essay voice. America handles the technical pattern data.
